blocks.content: The expenses, including salaries, allowances, and pensions of constitutional office holders, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.

items: Age Limit Distinction: Central constitutional heads retire at 65 years, whereas State Public Service Commission members retire at 62 years.
Voting in Parliament: Salaries charged on the Consolidated Fund of India are subject to discussion but not to the vote of Parliament.
Removal Authority: SPSC members are appointed by the Governor but can only be removed by the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tenure for standard constitutional heads such as the CAG, CEC, and UPSC Chairman is 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
Salaries, allowances, and pensions of constitutional posts are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable by Parliament.
Conditions of service cannot be varied to the disadvantage of the office holder after their appointment.
Resignation letters are addressed directly to the President of India for central constitutional posts.
